claims.claim: Short-obstruction equivalence and radius-three normal form: in a P8-free bipartite graph, a set S is a feedback vertex set exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. Moreover, every component of G-S has radius at most 3; if S is inclusion-minimal, every x in S has two neighbors in one component of G-S.
claims.evidence: Assume S is an FVS for the two normal-form clauses. If G-S has a cycle, a shortest such cycle is chordless; since all its vertices lie outside S, it is induced in G. It has even length. If its length is at least 10, eight consecutive vertices induce P8, a contradiction. Hence hitting induced C4, C6, and C8 is equivalent to deleting all cycles. Every component of G-S is then a tree. A diameter of at least seven edges would give an induced P8 in G, so its diameter is at most six and its radius at most three. If S is inclusion-minimal, restoring any x in S creates a cycle containing x; removing x from that cycle leaves a path in one component of G-S between two distinct neighbors of x.
claims.witness: The proof certificates are respectively a shortest residual cycle, a diametral tree path, and the cycle created by restoring an inclusion-essential vertex x.
claims.search_method: Direct proof from shortest cycles, hereditary induced paths, tree diameter, and inclusion-minimality; all scope and quantifiers were checked explicitly.

claims.claim: There is an exact parameterized algorithm running in O(8^k n^8) time for solutions of size at most k, as well as a polynomial-time 8-approximation.
claims.evidence: Enumerating all 4-, 6-, and 8-vertex subsets and retaining exactly those inducing cycles takes O(n^8) time. By claim 0, FVS solutions are exactly the transversals of this rank-eight hypergraph. Branching on every vertex of an uncovered hyperedge is exhaustive and has O(8^k) nodes up to a constant factor, giving O(8^k n^8) time. For approximation, scan the listed cycles to obtain a maximal vertex-disjoint family of p cycles. Its union U meets every listed cycle by maximality, hence is an FVS. Every FVS uses distinct vertices to meet the p disjoint cycles, so OPT is at least p, while |U| is at most 8p.
claims.witness: The branching tree and a maximal vertex-disjoint short-cycle packing provide constructive certificates for the exact decision algorithm and the approximation ratio.
claims.search_method: Independent recurrence, completeness, runtime, and packing-versus-transversal analysis.

claims.claim: Every C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has treewidth at most 13. Consequently, Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on this subclass.
claims.evidence: The standalone exact checker exhaustively extends every ordered bipartite graph containing the required path edges. Heredity makes prefix pruning complete, and every optional edge set is tried uniquely. It reproduced survivor counts 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0 for orders 1 through 15, proving that no valid graph contains a simple 15-vertex path. In an undirected DFS forest every edge has ancestor-comparable endpoints. Every root-to-leaf DFS path therefore has at most 14 vertices. Taking each vertex together with all its ancestors as a bag covers every edge, and the bags containing a fixed vertex form its descendant subtree; connecting component roots yields a tree decomposition of width at most 13. A nice-decomposition DP that stores deleted bag vertices and connectivity partitions of retained vertices exactly detects cycle creation. Since the width is fixed, this DP is polynomial.
claims.witness: The exhaustive order-15 survivor count is zero; the resulting DFS ancestor bags have size at most 14.
claims.search_method: Exact integer-bitmask exhaustive enumeration followed by a deductive DFS tree-decomposition and connectivity-partition DP proof.

claims.claim: More generally, Feedback Vertex Set is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum number r of vertices meeting every C4; a concrete bound is 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)}.
claims.evidence: At any node, every C4-transversal must contain a vertex of a selected uncovered C4, so four-way branching with iterative deepening finds a minimum transversal X of size r in O(4^r n^{O(1)}) time. The hereditary graph G-X is C4-free, P8-free, and bipartite, and claim 2 constructs a width-13 decomposition. Adding X to every bag gives width at most r+13. On a nice decomposition, a state consists of the deleted bag subset and a partition recording connectivity among retained boundary vertices; edge and join transitions discard exactly the combinations that form a cycle. There are at most 2^{r+14} times the Bell number of r+14 states, which is 2^{O(r log r)} after absorbing constants. Cost minimization therefore returns an exact FVS within the claimed bound.
claims.witness: A minimum C4-transversal X, the augmented width-(r+13) decomposition, and the optimum root DP state form a constructive certificate.
claims.search_method: Direct verification of the transversal branching invariant, decomposition augmentation, partition-state sufficiency, and state count.

claims.claim: Several natural routes from these reductions to the full result are blocked by explicit P8-free families: C4-transversal number is unbounded even after removing false twins; 2-connected C4-free blocks have unbounded order; and the short-cycle LP is not integral.
claims.evidence: In the half-graph H_n, all same-side neighborhoods are strictly nested and all neighborhoods are nonempty, so there are no false twins. It is 2K2-free and therefore P5-free. Retaining all B vertices and a_{n-1},a_n leaves no C4. Conversely, if the second-smallest retained A-index is j, at most one retained B-index is at least j; hence at most n+2 vertices remain, proving the exact C4-transversal number n-2. For the theta graph with m length-three u-v branches, every cycle consists of two branches and has length six; deletion of any vertex leaves the graph connected for m at least two. An induced path using both terminals has at most one extra vertex beyond each terminal, so it has at most six vertices. Thus these are 2-connected, C4-free, P8-free graphs of order 2m+2. In K_{3,3}, deleting one vertex leaves a C4 while deleting two vertices from one side leaves a forest, so the FVS optimum is two. Its only induced short cycles are C4s, and the exact assignment 1/4 to every vertex satisfies every constraint with objective 3/2, strictly below the integral optimum. The checker confirmed the half-graph formula through n=7, theta properties through m=8, and the K_{3,3} values using integer bitmasks and rational arithmetic.
claims.witness: The explicit witnesses are the false-twin-free half-graphs H_n, the length-three theta graphs for arbitrary m at least two, and K_{3,3} with uniform LP value 1/4.
claims.search_method: Symbolic family proofs plus exact finite bitmask enumeration and Fraction-valued LP verification.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a polynomial-time algorithm for Feedback Vertex Set on every P8-free bipartite graph. The draft does not provide one: O(8^k n^8) is exponential in the solution bound, the polynomial exact algorithm assumes C4-freeness, and the r-parameter algorithm is exponential in a C4-transversal parameter that the verified half-graphs show is unbounded on the target class. The 8-approximation also has weaker strength than the requested exact algorithm. These are nevertheless correct and material structural, approximation, subclass, and parameterized results, so they constitute valid partial progress. The final writeup expressly states these limitations and claims only PARTIAL resolution, making claimed_resolution accurate rather than overstated or understated.
